segments.text: Okay, is it — is this recording? Yeah, the little light's on. Okay, cool.
The projector's doing the thing again where it just shows the, uh, the blue screen with the little no-signal box bouncing around.
You have to unplug the HDMI and plug it back in. And then wiggle it. This room is cursed, everybody knows this room is cursed.
Presidio's been cursed since we moved in. Somebody should file a ticket with the, uh, with the building people.
I filed one. In, like, July.
Of course you did.
[laughter]
Okay — okay, it's up. It's up. Nobody touch the cable. How was everybody's long weekend? Anybody do anything fun for Labor Day?
I went up to Sonoma for my cousin's wedding, which was lovely, but I think I'm still, like, a little dehydrated. It was ninety-five degrees and they did the whole thing outside.
I did absolutely nothing. I reorganized my closet and I'm, like, weirdly proud of it. I found a jacket I thought I lost in, like, twenty twenty-two.
That's a good weekend, honestly. We tried to take the kids camping and it rained. In September. In California. Which I didn't think was legal.
Wait, it rained? Where were you?
Up near, um, near Truckee. It was like a twenty-minute thunderstorm and then my youngest refused to go back in the tent. So we came home Sunday. Anyway. Alex, you want to drive?

Yeah. So, the goal for today is pretty simple. I want us to walk out of here with a launch date for Route Planner v2 that we actually believe in. Not a, not a vibe, an actual date. And then owners on the handful of things that are blocking it.
I put a doc in the channel last night with the, the list. I'll put it up here. Sarah, do you want to start with where engineering is?

Sure. So, um — the big stuff is basically done. Multi-stop optimization is merged, the new constraint solver is behind the flag in staging, and the driver app sync, the offline sync thing, that landed last Thursday. So, like, the scary architecture stuff is behind us.

What's left is kind of a long tail. There's bulk import for depots, which is mostly done but the CSV validation is janky, like if you have a trailing comma it just silently drops the row. And then there's the ETA display on the dispatcher board, which we're still arguing about.
Arguing with who?
With ourselves, mostly. It's whether we show a range or a single time. Dana has opinions.

I do have opinions. Dispatchers hate ranges. Every single interview we did, they said just give me a time, and if it's wrong, tell me it's wrong. They don't want, like, two fifteen to three forty-five.
But if we show a single time and it's wrong, that's worse, right? Then we look —
No, but that's what the late-risk flag is for, that's the whole —
Okay, okay. Let's not solve that in here. Can you two just grab thirty minutes after this and land it? Whatever you two agree on, I'm fine with.
Yeah, fine.
Yep.
How's performance? Last time we looked the solver was kind of slow on the really big fleets.
It's better. It's not where I want it. On the big fleets it's, it's okay, it's not great. I've got someone profiling it this week. I don't think it blocks launch though, I think it's a follow-up.
Okay. And is there anything you're scared of? Like genuinely scared of. Not, like, polite scared.

Honestly? The stuff I'm scared of is the stuff we haven't tested much. We touched a lot of the address and geocoding path for multi-stop, and the regression coverage there is thin. But that's more a Priya question.

Yeah, so — that's exactly my worry, actually. We have good automation on the solver and on the driver app. But the address stuff, the geocoding stuff, that's mostly manual spot checks right now. Like, me typing addresses into staging and squinting at the map.
Okay. So what do you need?

I need a real regression test plan. Like, written down. Everything we're gonna run before we ship, including the ugly edge cases, the weird addresses, the — you know, the stuff that only breaks for one customer. Right now it's kind of in my head and in, like, three different spreadsheets.
Can you get that done this week?
Um. Yeah. Yeah, I think so. I can have the regression test plan done by Friday. Friday the eleventh.
Okay, great. So Priya, regression test plan, due Friday, September 11. I'm writing it down.
And it'll be in Notion. Not a spreadsheet. I promise.
Thank God.
Do you need anything from engineering for it? Like, do you need Sarah's team to review it?
I'll send it to Sarah once it's up, but I don't need a meeting. I just need, like, a list of what changed in the geocoding stuff so I know where to poke.
I can get you that today. It's basically one PR and then, like, four follow-ups.
Perfect.
Okay. Dana, design side.

So, um, most of the v2 screens are final. The dispatcher board is final, the route editor is final, the driver app screens were final like two weeks ago, Sarah's team has all of those. The big thing that's not done is onboarding.

Right now onboarding is still the v1 flow with a new coat of paint. And it doesn't — it doesn't really set anyone up for multi-stop. People land in the app and they have no idea they're supposed to import their depots first, so they just start drawing routes by hand, which is, like, the thing we're trying to kill.
That's the thing Marcus keeps complaining about, right? The, uh, the first-week drop-off?
Yeah, it's that. And I have sketches. I don't have real mockups. I have, like, boxes and arrows in Sigma.
What do you need to get to real mockups?

Honestly? Just time. I'm also doing the marketing site refresh, and that's eating, like, half my week. If I'm not doing the marketing site stuff, I could have the onboarding mockups done by — let's say Thursday the seventeenth? That gives me a week and a bit, and I want to put them in front of two or three customers before I call them done.
Is the seventeenth too late? If we're launching at the end of the month?

Not for us. Onboarding is mostly front end, it's not a ton of engineering. If we have the mockups on the seventeenth, we can build it in about a week. It's tight, but it's, it's doable. We already have the components.
Okay. So Dana, onboarding mockups, due Thursday, September 17. And I'll take the marketing site off your plate. I'll figure that out, that's on me.
Okay. Thank you. Seriously. Thank you.
Which customers are you thinking for the testing?
Probably a couple of the smaller carriers, the ones who onboarded in the last month or so, because they still remember how confusing it was. I'll ask CS for names.
Don't use anyone who's mad at us right now.
Ha. Yeah. Noted.

Can we make sure we put the analytics events in, too? Like, I want to actually know where people drop off in the new flow. Last time we shipped onboarding with no events and then we were just guessing for a month.
Yeah, I'll put the events in the spec. Sarah, can someone on your side sanity-check them?
Yeah, send them over.
Okay. So let's talk date. Because, honestly, that's why I'm here.
Yeah.

We've been saying, quote, end of September, for like two months now. I want a real date. I want to be able to tell customers a date, I want Marcus to be able to tell prospects a date, and I want it in the board deck.
So, if you're asking me, end of the month is realistic if regression doesn't turn up anything big. That's the, the caveat.
Sure. There's always a caveat.
I mean, it's a real caveat.
No, I know, I know. I'm not — I'm just saying.

From the QA side, if the plan's done Friday, I can run the full pass the week of the fourteenth, and then the week of the twenty-first is for, you know, fixes and a second pass. So that gets us to the end of the month.
That actually lines up. Two weeks of testing, and we launch right at the end of that.
Okay. Then let's lock September 30 for Route Planner v2 launch.
Works for me.
Yeah. Yep.
Yeah, that works. It's tight, but it works.
Great. September 30 it is. That's a Tuesday — no, wait. It's a Wednesday. September 30 is a Wednesday.
Wednesday's fine. Midweek is better for a launch anyway. Nobody reads anything on a Friday.
Okay. I'll update the roadmap doc and the launch page with the date.
And I'll put it in the board deck. Launch September 30.
Can we — sorry, can we just agree that if regression finds something real, we talk about it, instead of, like, everybody crunching to hit the date?
Yes. A hundred percent. I don't want anybody pulling all-nighters for this. If something real comes up, you tell me, and we talk about it. The date's not a, it's not a hostage situation.
Okay. Cool. Thank you.
Okay, next thing. Launch mechanics. Sarah, are we doing the flag rollout like we talked about? The percentage thing?

Yeah. So the plan is internal accounts first, then like ten percent of customers, then everybody over about a week. And we can flip it back per account if something goes sideways, so it's not all or nothing.
Which customers go first?
I was gonna say the small ones. Less, uh, less blast radius.
I'd actually argue the opposite. The big accounts are the ones who asked for multi-stop. If they don't get it first they're gonna be annoyed, and they're the ones who talk to each other.
But if it breaks for a big account, that's —
No, I hear you, I hear you.
Can we do a hybrid? Like, a couple of friendly big accounts who've opted in, plus the small ones? People who'd tell us if something's off instead of just churning.
Yeah, that's fine. I just need the list. Like, actual account IDs.
I'll get you the list from Marcus. That's easy.
Do we have a rollback plan written down? Like, not in Sarah's head?
Hey.
No offense.
None taken. It is in my head. I'll write it up. It's short, honestly, it's basically flip the flag and restore the old solver config, and then there's one migration we'd have to think about.
Which migration?

The saved routes. When someone opens an old saved route in v2 we convert it to the new format. If we roll back, the old app can still read it, we kept both fields, but I want to test that for real, not just, like, believe it.
I'll put that in the regression plan. Rollback with converted routes.
Thank you.
Okay, rollback plan written down before launch, that's Sarah. No hard date, just before launch.
Yep.
What about the driver app? Doesn't that have to go through the app store review thing?

Yeah, good call. The driver app update has to go through review on both stores. It's usually a day or two, but it's been slow lately, so I want to submit about a week before launch with the new stuff behind the flag.
Okay. Can you put that on the launch checklist so we don't forget?
Already there.
What about support? The support folks need to know this is coming. Last launch they found out from a customer, which was — that was bad.
Yeah, that was bad. I'll do a walkthrough for support the week before. I'll put something on the calendar. And we should give CS a, like, a one-pager they can send.
And release notes.
I can do the screenshots for release notes. I'm not writing them.
No, I'll write them. Well, I'll write a draft, and then somebody who writes better than me fixes it.
Low bar.
Thanks, John.
[laughter]
Okay, next thing on your list. The dashboard. The churn dashboard. That thing is still broken, right?
Yeah. So the churn dashboard is — the numbers look off. Some of the retention numbers look way too good. Like, suspiciously good. And I don't trust them.
I need that working before the board meeting. I'm not putting numbers in front of Tom that I don't trust.
Totally. It's Ben's. Ben built the pipeline for it.
Ben's not in yet, right? I think he said he was coming in late today.
Yeah, he's not here. I'll ask Ben to fix the churn dashboard. I'll ping him today.
Thank you.
Is that the same dashboard CS uses for renewals? Or is that a different one?
Same one, I think. Which is another reason to fix it.
Okay. What else is on the list?
Um, the bulk import, which Sarah already covered. The ETA thing, which Dana and Sarah are gonna fight about after this.
Discuss. We're going to discuss it.
Discuss. Sorry. And then pricing, which is really more a me-and-Marcus thing, but I want to flag it. We've got Acme tomorrow, and they're gonna ask about pricing for v2.
What are you gonna tell them?
I'm still working it out. I think per vehicle is where we land for fleets their size, but I want to think it through before I say anything on a call.
Okay. Loop me in before anything goes out in writing.
Yep. Will do.
And for the board — sorry, one more board thing. I'd love to have real v2 screenshots in the deck, not the, the mocks from the spring.
I can pull those from staging. Just tell me which screens.
The dispatcher board with a real multi-stop route on it. That's the money shot.
Okay. I'll grab it this week.
Make sure you use the demo account, not a real customer's routes.
Yes. Obviously. Demo account.
Anything else? Anything I'm missing?
Just — test environments. Staging data is like three months old. If I'm running the full regression pass the week of the fourteenth, I'd really like a fresh copy with, like, anonymized addresses.
That's a Ben thing too, I think. The anonymizing script is his.
Okay, I'll add it to my Ben list. Fresh anonymized staging data for Priya.
Thank you.

Okay. Let me just recap so it's in the, uh, in the recording. Launch is September 30 for Route Planner v2. Dana, onboarding mockups, Thursday the 17th. Priya, regression test plan, this Friday, the 11th.

Sarah, rollback plan written down before launch, driver app submitted about a week out, and you and Dana land the ETA display thing. And me — I'll ask Ben to fix the churn dashboard and get Priya fresh staging data, I'll get the rollout list from Marcus, and I'll set up the support walkthrough.
Good. That's a good meeting. We're giving everyone back, like, half an hour.
Wow.
A miracle.
Can I stay in here though? I have a call at eleven and every other room is booked.
It's all yours. Don't touch the HDMI.
Okay, stopping the recording.
